idea-plugin.name: Codebloom - Code Mind Maps
idea-plugin.description:
See any file as a pastel mind map of its classes and functions, with the real code on every branch and call arrows between them.

Long files are hard to read top to bottom, especially when much of the code was written with AI help. Codebloom lays a file out around its name so you can see its shape at a glance, open any block's code in place, and follow what it calls and what calls it, across the whole project.

  • Built on the IDE's code model. Blocks come from the Structure view and calls from IntelliJ's own resolution, so Java and Kotlin links are exact. Every language your IDE understands works.
  • Callers on demand. Select a block to find its callers anywhere in the project, including calls through interfaces and base classes.
  • Callbacks are not "unused". Methods passed as values (method references, handlers, registered nodes) are listed as Passed as a value.
  • Back and forward while you follow calls from file to file, with a trail of where you've been.
  • Copy as context puts a block, its calls and its callers on the clipboard for an AI chat.
  • Follows your editor and caret, matches your theme, runs fully locally with no telemetry.

Open it from the Codebloom tool window on the right, or Open Codebloom Map in the editor's context menu. Open Codebloom Map in Editor Tab opens the map as an editor tab instead, like any other file, so it can be split, dragged or given the whole editor.
